newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: San Miguel says CC-Amatil deal beneficial.
newsitem.headline: San Miguel says CC-Amatil deal beneficial.

text.p: Philippine food and beverage firm San Miguel Corp (SMC) said on Thursday its net income would be enhanced following the merger of its Coca-Cola subsidiary with Coca-Cola Amatil (CCA) of Australia.

"The impact of the merger on SMC's consolidated income is going to be positive this year and that positive number will be growing as we move along to the years 1998, 1999 and 2000," San Miguel chief financial officer Delfin Gonzalez said in a statement.
He did not give specific numbers.
Under the deal, which is expected to be completed in June, San Miguel will sell its 70 percent owned subsidiary, Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc, in exchange for a 25 percent stake in CCA.
The Sydney-based CCA is one of Coca-Cola's largest bottlers, operating in 17 countries with a total consumer base of 380 million.

News of the proposed merger sent San Miguel A and B shares down earlier this week as investors saw the deal as disadvantageous to San Miguel. Coca-Cola Bottlers is one of the most profitable subsidiaries of San Miguel.
On Thursday, San Miguel's A shares were unchanged at 53.50 pesos while its B shares rose 4.50 pesos to 80 pesos.

Gonzalez said aside from income from operations, San Miguel would receive additional income of about 420.4 million pesos every year for the next 10 years due to the "non-compete agreement" entered into by the two parties.
The non-compete agreement prohibits San Miguel from competing against CCA in the carbonated beverage market.
San Miguel will also be able to recognise up to 75 percent of profits from future container sales to Coca-Cola Bottlers, Gonzalez added.

At present, container sales to Coca-Cola Bottlers are eliminated upon consolidation of its financial statements as these containers are not considered sold but remain as assets in its operations, the company added.

"Since it will provide us substantial ownership in a key anchor bottler, we will thus be able to participate on a larger scale in the global growth of the Coca-Cola business, and we expect that the alliance will enhance San Miguel's net income in 1987 and beyond," San Miguel chief executive Andres Soriano III said in a statement.
